title: Kulabo mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Kulabo mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Kulabo mungbean is a mungbean variety from BPI NCRDC Los Baños, Laguna. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Kulabo is a registered mungbean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2004 as NSIC 2004 Mg 14. BPI NCRDC Los Baños, Laguna bred it. It takes about 58 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

**Yield:** 1.13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.
**Recommended for:** the areas in its trials, in both the wet and the dry season.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Kulabo mungbean takes about 58 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.13 t/ha trails the average of its group, 1.25. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 5.2 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is dull green. The seed holds 23.76 percent crude protein.
Where and when to plant Kulabo mungbean

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 58 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.13 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Kulabo?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
